Raw_Evidence_Span: Cu-12%-ANP exhibits very high yield and tensile strengths of 729 ± 27 and 1036 ± 35 MPa, respectively, along with relatively large uniform and total elongations of 7.2% ± 0.4% and 9.7% ± 0.4%, respectively.
Porosity-free bulk composite (density: >99.8%)
equiaxed, with ultrafine grains averaging to 0.39 ± 0.14 μm
amorphous B₄C nanoparticles (~47 nm in average diameter, up to 12% volume fraction)

Composition.Material_Name_Raw: Cu-12%-ANP (copper reinforced with amorphous B₄C nanoparticles, 12 vol.%)

Nominal_Composition.Note: Paper reports composition as matrix (high-purity Cu) + reinforcement (B₄C 12 vol.%). Full elemental composition not tabulated.

Measured_Composition.Note: APT measured nanoparticle composition: B₃.₈₉C with 8 at% Cu incorporated. This is local phase composition of nanoparticles, not bulk composition.

Composition.Note: Matrix is high-purity copper; reinforcement is B₄C nanoparticles at 12 vol.%. Gas-atomized copper powders (~30-35 μm) mixed with crystalline B₄C microparticles (2-4 μm).

Process_Text.original: Gas-atomized copper powders (average size of ~35 μm) were mixed with crystalline B₄C microparticles (average size of ~4 μm, 12 vol.%). A porosity-free bulk composite (density: >99.8%) was then built using L-PBF. The powder mixing was facilitated by using a high-shear dispersion facility (Nobilta, Hosokawa Micron Ltd., Japan) for 20 min at a rotation speed of 1600 rpm under the protection of argon. Composites were then built using a selective laser melting machine (S210, BLT, China) under high-purity argon to minimize oxidation (oxygen content: <50 ppm). This system was equipped with a single-mode fibre laser (500 W, 1064 nm wavelength) with a spot size of 60 μm. A cooling substrate system was designed in the printing machine to ensure a constant substrate temperature of ~20 °C during L-PBF to ensure a high cooling rate upon sample building, and a continuous scanning strategy involving a 67° rotation before scanning another layer was adopted.
Process_Text.simplified: Cu (~35 μm) + B₄C (~4 μm, 12 vol.%) powder mixed at 1600 rpm for 20 min under Ar. L-PBF (BLT S210, 500 W, 1064 nm, 60 μm spot, substrate ~20 °C, 67° layer rotation) under Ar (<50 ppm O₂).

equipped with HAADF-STEM; equipped with EDS: Bruker SuperX
used for TEM sample preparation via standard lift-out method

used for electrical conductivity measurement at room temperature

Processing.Note: As-built, no heat treatment applied. Oxygen content <50 ppm — upper bound, not exact. Exact scan speed, hatch spacing, layer thickness not in accessible text (referenced as Supplementary Table 1). Energy density for nanoscale refinement reported as 180.6 J/m³.

Structure_Text.original: The as-built bulk composite is porosity-free to near-full density (>99.8%), with densely and uniformly dispersed quasi-amorphous B₄C nanoparticles in an equiaxed ultrafine Cu matrix. Nanoparticles are amorphous as indicated by XRD and NMR, with nanocrystals (~2.9 nm, Cu) inside the amorphous nanoparticles. Copper grains are equiaxed, averaging 0.39 ± 0.14 μm. Grain sizes decrease from 7.17 ± 4.48 μm to 0.39 ± 0.14 μm with increasing particle volume fraction. No obvious texture in as-built samples. APT shows nanoparticle composition B₃.₈₉C with 8 at% Cu, and very limited diffusion of B and C atoms into copper (~5 nm). As-built dislocation density estimated at (2.3 ± 0.3) × 10¹⁴ m⁻² via modified Williamson-Hall method.
Structure_Text.simplified: Equiaxed ultrafine Cu grains (0.39 ± 0.14 μm) with dense quasi-amorphous B₄C nanoparticles (~47 nm avg, 12 vol.%). Near-full density >99.8%. Nanocrystals (~2.9 nm Cu) inside nanoparticles. No obvious texture. As-built dislocation density ~2.3 × 10¹⁴ m⁻².

Secondary_Phases.Note: Quasi-amorphous: contain ~2.9 nm Cu nanocrystals. Formed by in situ nano-fragmentation and melt-quench of crystalline B₄C microparticles.

Raw_Evidence_Span: Molecular dynamics simulations were performed using LAMMPS software to examine the interactions between dislocations and B₄C nanoparticles during deformation
The radii of the ANPs and CNPs were set to 3 nm

Composition.Material_Name_Raw: MD simulation model: Cu + B₄C nanoparticle (ANP)

Process_Text.original: MD simulations performed using LAMMPS. Cu-Cu: EAM potential; B-B, C-C, B-C: Stillinger-Weber potential; Cu-B, Cu-C: Lennard-Jones potential. Simulation cell: 38.2 × 22.1 × 25.0 nm, ~1.7 million atoms. Time step: 2 fs. Applied shear strain rate: 10⁷ s⁻¹.
Process_Text.simplified: MD simulation with LAMMPS, ~1.7M atoms, shear strain rate 10⁷ s⁻¹.

Structure_Text.original: ANP radius 3 nm embedded in Cu matrix with preexisting edge dislocations (b = a₀/2[101̄] on (111) plane). Simulation cell oriented X[101̄], Y[1̄2̄1], Z[111]. ANP generated by packing B₁₁C units and C-B-C chains.
Structure_Text.simplified: MD model: 3 nm radius ANP in Cu with edge dislocations on (111) plane.

Properties.Note: 原文: continuous decreases in configurational potential energy with applied strain (Fig. 4g). Exact values not accessible from text.

Experiment_Link.Description: MD simulation models dislocation-ANP interactions observed experimentally
Experiment_Link.Validation_Target: Dislocation absorption and stress delocalization at ANP interfaces

Composition.Material_Name_Raw: CPFE model: Cu + 12 vol.% B₄C nanoparticles
Composition.Note: CPFE model for 12 vol.% nanoparticles, calibrated with in situ XRD data from 8 vol.% sample.

Process_Text.original: Dual-phase crystal plasticity model: rate-dependent finite strain crystal plasticity for Cu matrix (12 {111}<110> slip systems), rate-independent J2 plasticity for B₄C nanoparticles. Uniaxial tension simulation at 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹. Solved using VUMAT in Abaqus/Explicit.
Process_Text.simplified: CPFE model: crystal plasticity for Cu + J2 plasticity for B₄C, in Abaqus/Explicit.

Structure_Text.original: Dual-phase model with Cu matrix and B₄C nanoparticles at 12 vol.%. Crystal plasticity constitutive model for Cu with power law hardening. Isotropic hardening plasticity for B₄C.
Structure_Text.simplified: CPFE dual-phase model: Cu matrix + 12 vol.% B₄C nanoparticles.

Properties.Note: 原文: ANPs demonstrate remarkably improved strain hardening, contributing to most (61%) of the strain hardening magnitude of Cu-ANP (true strain range 1% to 7%).

Experiment_Link.Description: CPFE model calibrated against in situ synchrotron XRD lattice strain data
Experiment_Link.Validation_Target: Simulated lattice strain responses match experimental data (Supplementary Fig. 10a)
